newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu decision signed and sealed - prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu decision signed and sealed - prosecutor.

text.p: Israel's state attorney Edna Arbel said on Sunday prosecutors had reached a decision on whether to charge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a corruption scandal, but she did not disclose what it was.

"Everything's already signed and sealed. I imagine that first of all, people who are involved must hear our decisions and afterwards the public will also know. The decision was hard and it's certainly not simple," Arbel told Israel Radio. An announcement was expected later in the day.
Netanyahu kept out of the public eye, even cancelling two appearances, while waiting to hear whether prosecutors would charge him in the scandal over his appointment of an attorney general.
All major Israeli newspapers and radio stations predicted Attorney General Elyakim Rubinstein would announce later in the day that Netanyahu would not be indicted. Rubinstein has the final say.

Netanyahu has described the influence-peddling scandal as "nonsense" and rejected calls to resign. If indicted on charges of fraud and breach of trust as recommended by police, he would still be under no legal obligation to quit.

Yet even if he is not indicted, a scathing report could prompt angry coalition partners to pull out, toppling his Likud-led coalition of mainly right-wing and religious parties which holds 66 seats in the 120-member parliament.
